record.original_question: For k > 1, does the property Mix(k) lift under a typical extension, where typicality is understood in the Halmos metric?

evidence.quote: В [19] доказано, что типичное (в метрике Халмоша) расширение всякого перемешивающего автоморфизма также обладает перемешиванием. Возникает вопрос о кратном перемешивании.
Q7. Поднимается ли свойство M ix(k), k > 1, при типичном расширении?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu)$ be a standard non-atomic Lebesgue probability space, and let $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ denote the group of all invertible measure-preserving transformations of $(X,\mu)$, equipped with the Halmos metric
$$d(S,T)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}2^{-n}\bigl(\mu(SA_n\triangle TA_n)+\mu(S^{-1}A_n\triangle T^{-1}A_n)\bigr),$$
where $\{A_n\}$ is a fixed countable dense subalgebra of $\mathcal{B}$. With this metric $\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ is a Polish space, and "typical" means "belonging to a dense $G_\delta$ set."

For an integer $k\ge 2$, a transformation $T\in\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ is said to be mixing of order $k$, written $T\in\mathrm{Mix}(k)$, if for every measurable sets $A_0,A_1,\dots,A_k\in\mathcal{B}$,
$$\lim_{\min_{i\ne j}|n_i-n_j|\to\infty}\mu\bigl(A_0\cap T^{-n_1}A_1\cap\cdots\cap T^{-n_k}A_k\bigr)=\prod_{i=0}^{k}\mu(A_i).$$

An extension of $T\in\mathrm{Aut}(X,\mu)$ is a transformation $\widetilde T\in\mathrm{Aut}(X\times Y,\mu\times\nu)$ on a product Lebesgue space such that $\widetilde T$ projects onto $T$ via the first coordinate; the set of such extensions is itself a Polish space in the induced Halmos metric.

Question: For $k>1$, is it true that for every $T\in\mathrm{Mix}(k)$, a typical (in the sense of Baire category with respect to the Halmos metric) extension $\widetilde T$ of $T$ also belongs to $\mathrm{Mix}(k)$?
artifact.category_tag: ergodic theory: higher-order mixing and generic extensions
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in lecture notes by Ryzhikov on ergodic transformations. While it is known that a typical extension of a mixing automorphism is mixing (the case k=1), and there are related results on k-fold mixing lifting to weakly mixing isometric extensions and on generic properties of extensions, no resolution for Mix(k) under typical extensions for k>1 in the Halmos metric was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: Lecture notes on ergodic transformations (Ryzhikov)
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open questions on higher-order mixing and generic/typical extensions in the Halmos metric.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is stated as an open question regarding lifting of Mix(k) under typical extensions.

status_evidence.title: k-fold mixing lifts to weakly mixing isometric extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Result on lifting k-fold mixing to certain classes of extensions (isometric, weakly mixing).
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for special kinds of extensions, but not for the typical extension in the Halmos sense.

status_evidence.title: Generic properties of extensions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies genericity of various mixing-type properties for extensions.
status_evidence.claim: Related genericity results for extensions exist but do not resolve Mix(k) lifting for k>1.
